classification.difficultyReason: Requires discovering a suitable centre and common sum, using complementary opposite pairs, and arranging those pairs to satisfy the perimeter constraints simultaneously, with no strategy supplied.

content.prompt: Place the numbers 1 to 13 in the circles in the following figure so that the sums of the numbers on each straight line are equal.

spec.description: Flat-topped hexagon with circles at its six vertices, six side midpoints and centre. Six perimeter lines and six diameters each contain three circles. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Thirteen blank circles; numbers 1 through 13 are to be used once each so all twelve three-circle line sums agree.
spec.answerVisibility: All circles remain empty in the question edition.

answer.short: One solution is shown. Every straight line sums to $21$.
answer.worked:
Put $7$ in the centre. Pair the remaining numbers to total $14$: $(1,13)$, $(2,12)$, $(3,11)$, $(4,10)$, $(5,9)$ and $(6,8)$. Place each pair opposite across the centre, then arrange the pairs so the perimeter lines also total $21$.

Checks for the six perimeter lines, clockwise from the top:
$$\begin{align*}8+10+3&=21\\3+5+13&=21\\13+2+6&=21\\6+4+11&=21\\11+9+1&=21\\1+12+8&=21\end{align*}$$
Checks for the six lines through the centre:
$$\begin{align*}8+7+6&=21\\10+7+4&=21\\3+7+11&=21\\5+7+9&=21\\13+7+1&=21\\2+7+12&=21\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: Each integer 1 through 13 occurs once; all twelve straight lines sum to 21.
